title: One Hundred Years of Solitude (Cien años de soledad)
summary: Gabriel García Márquez's novel follows seven generations of the Buendía family in the invented town of Macondo. Editorial Sudamericana published it in Buenos Aires in 1967, after he offered the manuscript in 1965. The Nobel Foundation calls it his international breakthrough.

uncertainty.note: Year of first publication; a corrected typescript page at the Harry Ransom Center is dated 1966 and García Márquez offered the manuscript to the publisher in 1965 (Paris Atlas).

as_recorded.value: Cien años de soledad. Buenos Aires: Ed. Sudamericana, 1967.
Editorial Sudamericana published it in Buenos Aires in 1967.

where.modern_name: Buenos Aires, Argentina (pin: place of first publication; the author had moved to Mexico City in 1961 and the place of writing is not stated on pages opened)

importance.justification: The Nobel Foundation names it as García Márquez's international breakthrough.
